text:
Maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector rollout yesterday we're seeing a sustained host CPU uplift (~18% p50) on the ingest tier. Traces point to an extra ~120us per-request on the pre-tokenize path.
Ben: I saw that on graphs. Any flamegraphs yet?
Maya: yes, attached sample from a hot host: tokenization_utf8_normalize shows up as a big block. Looks like our normalization fast-path wasn't hitting for a subset of client inputs (emoji + non-ascii).
Sam: interesting. Which code path is doing normalization? Is this on the host preproc or in the tokenizer binary?
Maya: host preproc (go middleware) — we added a unicode.NFC normalization step in the grpc request parsing to unify user text before tokenization. It was meant to help model token stability but it's running on every request.
Diego: oof. That explains the p50. Normalization is O(n) and we've got many tiny requests. Did the kernel selector change cause more requests to hit the host preproc (vs offloaded path)?
Maya: yes — routing tweak sent more short chat-like requests to the optimized cpu-packed nodepool, which kept them on host preproc rather than fast-path sidecar. Net effect: more requests hit our normalization hotpath (~350k req/day -> ~1.2M).
Ben: any quick wins? Can we short-circuit NFC for ASCII-only payloads?
Sam: we already had an ascii fast-path in tokenizer, just not in the normalize step. Proposal: move normalization after a cheap ascii check and only normalize when necessary. Also batch normalize across request bundles when autoscaling batches requests (reduce per-request overhead).
Maya: did a quick patch on a dev host to gate normalize with an ascii check. Perf probe before/after:
```# dev host microbench (100k short requests)
baseline: avg host preproc 340us
with unicode.NFC on all: 460us (+35%)
with ascii-gate: 355us (+4%)
```
Maya: ascii-gate gets us most of the benefit.
Diego: good. What about gRPC/writev overhead while streaming? Any correlation with smaller writes after normalization change?
Maya: yes — traces show higher writev syscall counts per response. Smaller chunk sizes after normalization + tokenization order caused grpc to flush more frequently. p99 write syscall rate went up ~2x on the same hosts.
perf-bot: CPU profile attached: top stacks -> host.preproc.normalize -> tokenizer.tokenize -> grpc.Writev -> net.Write
Ben: Can we coalesce small frames at the host proxy layer? There was a previous patch that coalesced writes for http2, but not for grpc streaming.
Sam: grpc library has a WriteFlags/NO_PUBLISH option in streaming that we could use to batch a few small writes, but it's risky for latency. Maybe a heuristic: if response size < 128 bytes and client supports streaming aggregation, buffer up to 3 fragments or 10ms.
Diego: 10ms buffer could be okay for chat turn aggregation but risky for low-latency apps. We should make it configurable per route/model. Redwood Console could expose 'small-write-coalesce' flag per route.
Maya: action plan I'm proposing: 1) revert kernel-selector routing tweak for the small-host tier (rollback in 1hr) to stop the immediate pressure; 2) push ascii-gate minimal change to host preproc (fast rollbackable); 3) experiment with grpc write coalescing behind a route flag in canary; 4) add a perf test for unicode-heavy vs ascii-heavy workloads.
Ben: +1. Also add telemetry: histogram of writev bytes-per-call and count of normalization hits per-request. We don't have the latter currently.
Maya: added a lightweight counter in dev branch. Perf numbers look promising.
infra-bot: deploy request queued: maya/utf8-gate -> staging (dry-run) by infra on 1829994600.
Maya: staging dry-run passed. CPU p50 on staging improved from 420ms to 380ms for the sampled synthetic chat traffic.
Sam: for the grpc coalesce experiment, can we implement a server-side buffering layer that groups writes per connection but bounded by N messages or T milliseconds? Keep backpressure semantics intact.
Diego: yes — implement as middleware between tokenizer and grpc stream writer. Use a tiny ring buffer and drain on flush conditions. Propose defaults: N=4 or T=8ms. Include metrics for 'coalesced_writes' and 'coalesce_latency_added'.
Ben: note: we must check TLS socket Nagle interactions. writev + small delays can interact badly with tcp_nodelay. Ensure coalescing doesn't re-enable Nagle.
Maya: good catch. We'll keep tcp_nodelay true and coalesce at application level.
Maya: quick sample of coalesce heuristic pseudo:
```if payload_size < 128 and route_flags.coalesce_enabled {
  buffer.append(payload)
  if buffer.count >= N or buffer.age >= T {
    stream.writev(buffer.concat())
    buffer.clear()
  }
} else {
  stream.writev(payload)
}
```
Maya: timeline: ascii-gate patch -> canary in next 30m, rollback window 1h. If stable, gate to prod after perf confirm. Coalesce feature -> spike canary next week with route flag.
perf-bot: regression alert suppressed (temporary) — monitoring will watch writev rate and normalize-hit rate.
Ben: leave a note for product: normalization changed token distributions slightly for rare inputs; need to run evals to make sure model outputs not degraded.
Maya: yes, queued eval job for the top 1k prompt shards.
Sam: sounds good. Anything else?
Diego: can we also add a metric for "preproc_cpu_ms_per_req" broken down by ascii vs non-ascii? That will help future rollouts.
Maya: will add.
Ben: thanks everyone. @Maya please ping when the canary shows green so we can flip routing back permanently with the ascii-gate in place. :thumbsup:
Maya: will do.
